summary: Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University as an associate professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014).

Masaaki Sugiyama (1952–2019) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University (~1989–1992).
Masaaki Tsuchiya (born 1960) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1980–1988) and held a post at Senshu University around 1996.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, later serving as professor (1904) and library director (~1923–1934) at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He earned his doctorate from Tokyo University of Education (~1968–1977) and became an associate professor at Ibaraki University (1977) and professor emeritus at Tsukuba (2006).

Masahide Mori (born 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and Tibetology. He earned degrees from Nagoya University and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later serving as an associate professor (~1999–2009) and professor (~2009–2024) at Kanazawa University.
Masahide Tsujimura is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at Kyoto University and served as an assistant professor at Kobe University in 2013.
Masahiro Asada (born 1945) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1973) and later served there as an associate professor (~1985–1995).

Masahiro Inami (born 1960) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed graduate coursework at Hiroshima University (~1983–1989) and held teaching positions at Tokyo Gakugei University from around 1997.

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921–2009) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Tohoku University (~1944–1953), where he later served as professor and chair of religious studies and history of religion (~1973–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda (born 1957) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Tsukuba, Delhi, and TMU, serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and Musashino University (2023).
Masahiro Takano (born 1960) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1988–1993), where he was later attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita (born 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1975) and served there as head of the History of Japanese Philosophy department (~2003–2014).

Masakazu Tanaka (born 1955) works in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at Tohoku University and earned a Ph.D. from LSE/University of London, later serving as an associate professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019).

Masako Keta (born 1953) works in philosophy and religious studies. She completed her studies at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi and served as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai (1934–2000) was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1964) and later held an academic post there (~1968–1998).

Masamichi Ichigo (born 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani, Kyoto, Washington, and Michigan under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama, later serving as professor at Otani (1997) and president of Kyoto Koka Women's University (2007).
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Vienna, where he studied under Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University as a lecturer (attested 1991) and associate professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002).

Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).
